label: D2 arrival at S2 while the agent still prefers a1 (believes S1 is good)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (DELAY_2), and only when the reached state shown is S2 (100% of mass in_state==2); never at D1 or GO, never on S1. Within S2 arrivals it needs the agent to hold a moderate a1 preference (policy logit choice in about [2.8, 8) at that step; none fires at choice > 8.07 or below -1.5). Most firings (94%) are rare a1->S2 transitions, which is why it looks like a rare-transition detector, but the strongest activations are common a2->S2 arrivals while S1 is the good state, i.e. reaching S2 when the agent believes S1 is good. It fades over the episode and is almost silent after trial 80 (ep_trial < 80 lifts precision from 0.66 to 0.80). Magnitude tracks the a1 preference (coverage of choice>2.78 goes from 0.58 in the lowest activation quartile to 0.94 in the top). The observed-only version (D2 & state==2 & action==1) has recall 0.95 but precision 0.24. All variables used are observed or computed by the agent at D2; choice is the model policy readout, so the predicate partly restates the hidden belief.

issues: False claim: 'the strongest activations are common a2->S2 arrivals while S1 is good'. Within every activation quartile, D2 & state==2 & action==2 covers only 4-7% of firings (top quartile 0.069), while action==1, i.e. the rare a1->S2 transition, covers 93% (top quartile 0.931). So the top activations are rare a1->S2 arrivals. The a2->S2 & good==1 subset has precision 0.022 and mass recall 0.044.

The label's 'believes S1 is good' is not supported by the hidden good state. Adding good==1 to D2 & S2 & a1 gives F1 0.39, vs 0.386 without it. Adding it to the recorded predicate lowers dev F1 from 0.80 to 0.69. 14% of firings occur when good==2 or is unknown.

Nearly all of the selectivity comes from choice, which is the model's own logit(a1)-logit(a2) read out at the same D2 step. It cuts D2 & S2 & a1 (45,685 steps, precision 0.24) down to about 14,000 steps. The best predicate from observed variables only (D2 & S2 & a1 & ep_trial<60) reaches just F1 0.47. So the predicate mostly restates the hidden state instead of explaining it from inputs.
The 'choice < 8.07' bound in the explanation does nothing. At D2 on S2, choice is never >= 5 (0 steps predicted), and choice < -1.5 never fires (correct).

Confirmed: the unit fires only at D2 and only on S2 (100% of activation mass), never at D1 or GO. It is essentially silent for ep_trial >= 80 (mass recall 0.002). Magnitude increases strongly early in the episode: ep_trial<40 covers 90% of the top quartile but 31% of the bottom quartile.

Systematic false positives: firings after an a2 trial (prev_action==2). Excluding them raises dev precision from 0.80 to 0.84 at the same recall, which points to a recency effect from the previous choice.
The recorded test F1 of 0.788 is below the 0.8 bar.
